Marissa — thanks for the follow-up and the demo today. High level answers below, happy to provide more granularity if helpful.

1) Expected monthly tokens: ~120,000,000 tokens/month (this is prompts + responses; most calls are short).
2) Traffic profile: peak expected concurrency is ~40 RPS during weekday daytime. Average payload is roughly 150 tokens per request, so that maps to ~6,000 tokens/sec peak (40 * 150). Burstiness: we see short 10–15 minute spikes at that level.
3) Budget: for the first 3 months we’re looking at a target range of $8k–$15k/month (we need to get to a predictable unit cost). Our procurement target is to get to roughly $40–$60 per 1M tokens, ideally lower if volume/prior-commit discounts apply.
4) Compliance: data residency in US only, SOC 2 required (we have the questionnaire on file). SLA: standard 99.9% should be fine for initial pilot.

Question for you: given that peak TPS is bursty, do you have guidance on how hosted pricing handles bursts (is there burst capacity pricing vs steady-state)? Also, if we adopt some caching/prefix KV, how materially would that move the unit cost?

I’m copying procurement to loop them in on commercial.

Thanks,

Hi Samir — great, thanks for the details — that’s exactly what I needed. Quick notes inline and next steps: 

- Volume + unit economics: with 120M tokens/month and your target of ~$40–$60 per 1M, hosted is a good fit. For context, our standard hosted rate for comparable usage starts at $32 / 1M tokens and steps down with volume/commits. For a 3-month pilot at 120M/mo we can model a blended rate and explore a pilot discount.

- Peak/burst handling: hosted has built-in burst capacity; we provision steady-state capacity for the committed level and allow short bursts on top. Bursts are metered; they do not automatically require a dedicated reserve unless sustained. We can propose an autoscaling/burst allowance in the MPA.

- Cost reduction levers: caching (prefix/KV) and batching typically reduce billable tokens by 15–45% depending on your prompt patterns. If you expect a lot of repetitive prompts, prefix caching is highly effective.

Attachments: I’m attaching a mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) and an updated pricing worksheet. I’ll also publish a HubSpot deal with the assumptions so procurement can review.

Proposed commercial next steps:
1) I’ll model three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) for token volume and provide per-1M pricing and monthly totals.
2) I can offer a pilot package: 30% off list for first month + ability to convert to committed reserved capacity with a volume discount if you want predictable unit economics.
3) If procurement confirms the budget range, we’ll share an MPA and a DocuSign link to execute.

Would you like me to prioritize: (A) fastest time-to-pilot (get you live under hosted with pilot credits), or (B) go straight to committed reserved capacity pricing for better unit costs?

If you confirm (A) or (B) I’ll run numbers and send a formal proposal by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks — cc’ing Neha on procurement coordination.
